dc.description.abstract.value:
This guideline provides evidence-informed recommendations for the prevention and diagnosis of rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease, conditions that remain significant causes of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries and among vulnerable populations. Rheumatic heart disease, which affected an estimated 55 million people globally in 2021, arises from untreated or recurrent group A streptococcal infections and is closely associated with socioeconomic determinants such as poverty, overcrowding and limited access to health care. The document aims to support countries in reducing disease burden through improved early detection, timely treatment and effective prevention strategies.

Developed in accordance with WHO guideline methodology, the publication synthesizes current scientific evidence and expert consensus to formulate recommendations on primary and secondary prevention and selected aspects of clinical management. It addresses key areas including diagnosis and treatment of streptococcal pharyngitis and skin infections, use of echocardiography for diagnosis and screening, and antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent recurrence. The guideline places particular emphasis on populations at moderate to high risk and includes considerations for implementation, monitoring and adaptation in different settings. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers and health-care providers, it supports the development of national policies and clinical protocols to improve prevention, diagnosis and care.

dc.description.abstract.value:
This web annex presents systematic review reports that underpin the development of WHO recommendations on the prevention and diagnosis of rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease. It compiles and synthesizes available evidence addressing key clinical and public health questions structured according to PICO frameworks, including the effectiveness of health education interventions delivered by health-care workers to improve knowledge and promote the use of preventive health services in high-risk populations. The document contributes to the evidence base supporting guideline recommendations and is made publicly available to ensure transparency in the guideline development process.

The annex describes the objectives, methods and findings of individual systematic reviews conducted in accordance with established standards, including comprehensive literature searches, study selection, risk of bias assessment and grading of the certainty of evidence. It presents evidence profiles and summary of findings tables, alongside narrative syntheses where quantitative pooling is not feasible. Key outcomes assessed include changes in knowledge, health service utilization and intervention effects across diverse populations. The document also discusses methodological limitations and evidence gaps, highlighting areas requiring further research. It is intended for researchers, methodologists and stakeholders seeking detailed insight into the evidence informing the guideline.

dc.description.abstract.value: Globally rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is the leading cause of preventable cardiac death in people under the age of 25. RHD is caused by infection with Streptococcus A (Strep A) a widespread bacterium associated with infections that commonly occur in childhood. Untreated throat (and possibly skin) infection with Strep A (“strep throat”) triggers an autoimmune response in some children which then causes acute rheumatic fever (RF). RF affects the joints skin nervous system and heart. While patients with RF will typically recover the damage caused to the heart valves is permanent and can cause heart failure stroke heart rhythm problems and maternal death during pregnancy.Once a child is identified as having experienced RF regular antibiotic prophylaxis is required to prevent subsequent Strep A infections and consequent RF episodes which would further damage the heart.The vast majority of RF/RHD occurs in developing countries.It is a disease of poverty that is strongly associated with overcrowded living conditions.Available data indicate that RF/RHD presents a significant ongoing public health burden in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region. In May 2018 the World Health Assembly passed resolution WHA71.14 to prioritize action to address the global burden of RF/RHD. This regional framework for action on RF/RHD aims to guide implementation of this resolution in the Region.The framework was endorsed by Member States in resolution EM/RC66/R.1 of the WHO Regional Committee for the Eastern Mediterranean at the Committee’s 66th session in October 2019.

dc.description.abstract.value:
This web annex provides detailed documentation of the processes, methods and key questions underpinning the development of WHO recommendations on the prevention and diagnosis of rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease. It is made publicly available to ensure transparency and methodological rigour, describing procedures followed in accordance with the WHO handbook for guideline development, including scope definition, formulation of key questions, systematic evidence reviews and assessment of the certainty of evidence.

The document outlines the roles and contributions of the groups involved in the guideline development process, including the WHO Steering Group, the Guideline Development Group, systematic review teams and external reviewers, as well as processes for managing conflicts of interest and achieving consensus. It describes the use of structured approaches such as PICO frameworks, GRADE methods and evidence-to-decision frameworks to inform recommendations, and details the criteria used to determine their strength and direction. The annex also presents the full set of key clinical and public health questions that guided the evidence reviews. It is intended for researchers, methodologists, policy-makers and other stakeholders seeking to understand the methodological basis of the guideline.
